lessons.name: Words that rhyme
lessons.intro: Rhyming words have the same ending sound. Listen to cat and hat. Their beginning sounds are different, but their endings match.
lessons.rule: Rhyming words have the same ending sound. Listen to cat and hat. Their beginning sounds are different, but their endings match.

items.prompt: Which word rhymes with cat?
items.explanation: Cat and hat have the same ending sound.

items.prompt: Which word rhymes with pin?
items.explanation: Pin and fin have the same ending sound.

items.prompt: Which word rhymes with log?
items.explanation: Log and dog have the same ending sound.

items.prompt: Which word rhymes with sun?
items.explanation: Sun and run have the same ending sound.

items.prompt: Which word rhymes with bed?
items.explanation: Bed and red have the same ending sound.

items.prompt: Which word rhymes with cake?
items.explanation: Cake and lake have the same ending sound.

lessons.name: Same starting sound
lessons.intro: Listen to map and moon. They start with the same sound. Listen to each choice and find another word with the same beginning sound.
lessons.rule: Listen to map and moon. They start with the same sound. Listen to each choice and find another word with the same beginning sound.

items.prompt: Which word starts with the same sound as map?
items.explanation: Map and moon begin with the same sound.

items.prompt: Which word starts with the same sound as sun?
items.explanation: Sun and sock begin with the same sound.

items.prompt: Which word starts with the same sound as fish?
items.explanation: Fish and fan begin with the same sound.

items.prompt: Which word starts with the same sound as dog?
items.explanation: Dog and duck begin with the same sound.

items.prompt: Which word starts with the same sound as cat?
items.explanation: Cat and cup begin with the same sound.

items.prompt: Which word starts with the same sound as ship?
items.explanation: Ship and shop begin with the same sound. Sock and chip start differently.

lessons.name: Word beats
lessons.intro: A syllable is a beat in a spoken word. Sun has one beat. Rabbit has two. Banana has three. Say a word slowly and clap its beats.
lessons.rule: A syllable is a beat in a spoken word. Sun has one beat. Rabbit has two. Banana has three. Say a word slowly and clap its beats.

items.prompt: Say sun. How many syllables do you hear?
items.explanation: Sun has one syllable.

items.prompt: Say rabbit. How many syllables do you hear?
items.explanation: Rabbit has two syllables: rab, bit.

items.prompt: Say banana. How many syllables do you hear?
items.explanation: Banana has three syllables: ba, na, na.

items.prompt: Say sunset. How many syllables do you hear?
items.explanation: Sunset has two syllables: sun, set.

items.prompt: Say picnic. How many syllables do you hear?
items.explanation: Picnic has two syllables: pic, nic.

items.prompt: Say elephant. How many syllables do you hear?
items.explanation: Elephant has three syllables: el, e, phant.

lessons.name: Short a
lessons.intro: Let's practise short a words, like cat, map, and sat. Tap each word to hear it. Read it aloud. Then try the practice.
lessons.rule: Let's practise short a words, like cat, map, and sat.

lessons.name: Short i
lessons.intro: Let's practise short i words, like pin, sit, and pig. Tap each word to hear it. Read it aloud. Then try the practice.
lessons.rule: Let's practise short i words, like pin, sit, and pig.

lessons.name: Short o
lessons.intro: Let's practise short o words, like dog, log, and hop. Tap each word to hear it. Read it aloud. Then try the practice.
lessons.rule: Let's practise short o words, like dog, log, and hop.

lessons.name: Short u
lessons.intro: Let's practise short u words, like sun, cup, and bug. Tap each word to hear it. Read it aloud. Then try the practice.
lessons.rule: Let's practise short u words, like sun, cup, and bug.

lessons.name: Short e
lessons.intro: Let's practise short e words, like hen, bed, and ten. Tap each word to hear it. Read it aloud. Then try the practice.
lessons.rule: Let's practise short e words, like hen, bed, and ten.

lessons.name: Mix the vowels
lessons.intro: Now mix the short vowels. Look closely at the middle letter. Cat. Sit. Dog. Sun. Hen. Tap a word to hear it, then read it aloud.
lessons.rule: Now mix the short vowels. Look closely at the middle letter. Cat. Sit. Dog. Sun. Hen.

lessons.name: The sh team
lessons.intro: In these words, s and h work together to spell one sound. Ship. Shop. Fish. Sometimes the team is at the start. Sometimes it is at the end. Tap a word to hear it.
lessons.rule: In these words, s and h work together to spell one sound. Ship. Shop. Fish. Sometimes the team is at the start. Sometimes it is at the end.

lessons.name: The ch team
lessons.intro: In these words, c and h work together to spell one sound. Chip. Chop. Chin. Much. Tap a word to hear it. Then read the whole word aloud.
lessons.rule: In these words, c and h work together to spell one sound. Chip. Chop. Chin. Much.

lessons.name: More letter teams
lessons.intro: Meet two more letter teams. T and h work together in thin and moth. C and k work together at the end of duck and sock. Each team spells one sound in these words. Tap a word to hear it.
lessons.rule: Meet two more letter teams. T and h work together in thin and moth. C and k work together at the end of duck and sock. Each team spells one sound in these words.

lessons.name: Blends at the start
lessons.intro: In a blend, each letter keeps its sound. Stop. Clap. Frog. Read every letter, then put the sounds together. Tap a word to hear it.
lessons.rule: In a blend, each letter keeps its sound. Stop. Clap. Frog. Read every letter, then put the sounds together.

lessons.name: Blends at the end
lessons.intro: Now look for blends at the end. Lamp. Hand. Tent. Read all the way to the last letter. Each letter in a blend keeps its sound. Tap a word to hear it.
lessons.rule: Now look for blends at the end. Lamp. Hand. Tent. Read all the way to the last letter. Each letter in a blend keeps its sound.

lessons.name: Silent e: long a
lessons.intro: In these words, the last e is silent. The a has its long sound, like its letter name. Compare cap and cape. Tap a word to hear it. Read the whole word aloud.
lessons.rule: In these words, the last e is silent. The a has its long sound, like its letter name. Compare cap and cape.

lessons.name: Silent e: long i
lessons.intro: In these words, the last e is silent. The i has its long sound, like its letter name. Compare pin and pine. Tap a word to hear it. Read the whole word aloud.
lessons.rule: In these words, the last e is silent. The i has its long sound, like its letter name. Compare pin and pine.

lessons.name: Silent e: long o
lessons.intro: In these words, the last e is silent. The o has its long sound, like its letter name. Compare hop and hope. Tap a word to hear it. Read the whole word aloud.
lessons.rule: In these words, the last e is silent. The o has its long sound, like its letter name. Compare hop and hope.

lessons.name: Silent e: long u
lessons.intro: In these words, the last e is silent. Listen to cube and flute. Long u can sound like its letter name or like the vowel in flute. Tap a word to hear it. Read the whole word aloud.
lessons.rule: In these words, the last e is silent. Listen to cube and flute. Long u can sound like its letter name or like the vowel in flute.

lessons.name: Long a teams
lessons.intro: In these words, a i and a y spell long a. The a y team is at the end of play and stay. Tap a word to hear it. Read the whole word aloud.
lessons.rule: In these words, a i and a y spell long a. The a y team is at the end of play and stay.

lessons.name: Long e teams
lessons.intro: In these words, e e and e a spell long e. The e a team can spell other sounds in other words. Today we practise team and seat. Tap a word to hear it. Read the whole word aloud.
lessons.rule: In these words, e e and e a spell long e. The e a team can spell other sounds in other words. Today we practise team and seat.

lessons.name: Long o teams
lessons.intro: In these words, o a and o w spell long o. The o w team can have another sound in other words. Here we practise snow and grow. Tap a word to hear it. Read the whole word aloud.
lessons.rule: In these words, o a and o w spell long o. The o w team can have another sound in other words. Here we practise snow and grow.

lessons.name: The oo in moon
lessons.intro: Listen to moon and food. In these words, the o o team spells the same vowel sound. Read each whole word. Tap a word to hear it. Read the whole word aloud.
lessons.rule: Listen to moon and food. In these words, the o o team spells the same vowel sound. Read each whole word.

lessons.name: The oo in book
lessons.intro: Listen to book and look. The o o team has a different sound from moon. All the words in this lesson use the sound in book. Tap a word to hear it. Read the whole word aloud.
lessons.rule: Listen to book and look. The o o team has a different sound from moon. All the words in this lesson use the sound in book.

lessons.name: The ar team
lessons.intro: The letter r changes the vowel sound in these words. Listen to car, park, and star. Look for the a r team. Tap a word to hear it. Read the whole word aloud.
lessons.rule: The letter r changes the vowel sound in these words. Listen to car, park, and star. Look for the a r team.

lessons.name: The or team
lessons.intro: The letter r changes the vowel sound in these words. Listen to fork, corn, and storm. Look for the o r team. Tap a word to hear it. Read the whole word aloud.
lessons.rule: The letter r changes the vowel sound in these words. Listen to fork, corn, and storm. Look for the o r team.

lessons.name: Three ways to spell it
lessons.intro: Listen to her, bird, and turn. In these words, e r, i r, and u r spell the same vowel sound in this voice. Look closely at each spelling. Tap a word to hear it. Read the whole word aloud.
lessons.rule: Listen to her, bird, and turn. In these words, e r, i r, and u r spell the same vowel sound in this voice. Look closely at each spelling.

lessons.name: The oi and oy teams
lessons.intro: Listen to coin and toy. The vowel sound moves as you say it. O i and o y can spell that sound. O y is at the end of toy and boy. Tap a word to hear it. Read the whole word aloud.
lessons.rule: Listen to coin and toy. The vowel sound moves as you say it. O i and o y can spell that sound. O y is at the end of toy and boy.

lessons.name: The sound in cow
lessons.intro: Listen to out and cow. In these words, o u and o w spell the same vowel sound. These spellings can have other sounds in other words. Tap a word to hear it. Read the whole word aloud.
lessons.rule: Listen to out and cow. In these words, o u and o w spell the same vowel sound. These spellings can have other sounds in other words.

lessons.name: The c in city
lessons.intro: In these words, c sounds like s. This often happens before e, i, or y. Listen to city and face. Read each whole word. Tap a word to hear it. Read the whole word aloud.
lessons.rule: In these words, c sounds like s. This often happens before e, i, or y. Listen to city and face. Read each whole word.

lessons.name: The g in gem
lessons.intro: In these words, g sounds like j. It often has this sound before e, i, or y, but there are exceptions. Listen to gem and page. Tap a word to hear it. Read the whole word aloud.
lessons.rule: In these words, g sounds like j. It often has this sound before e, i, or y, but there are exceptions. Listen to gem and page.

lessons.name: Add ing
lessons.intro: An ending can add meaning. Jumping means doing the action of jump. These words add i n g without changing the base word. Look for the base and the ending. Tap a word to hear it. Read the whole word aloud.
lessons.rule: An ending can add meaning. Jumping means doing the action of jump. These words add i n g without changing the base word. Look for the base and the ending.

lessons.name: More than one
lessons.intro: These words name more than one. We often add s. After endings like x or sh, we add e s. Listen to cat and cats, box and boxes. Tap a word to hear it. Read the whole word aloud.
lessons.rule: These words name more than one. We often add s. After endings like x or sh, we add e s. Listen to cat and cats, box and boxes.

lessons.name: It already happened
lessons.intro: The ending e d can show that something already happened. It has different sounds in jumped, played, and wanted. The spelling stays e d. Tap a word to hear it. Read the whole word aloud.
lessons.rule: The ending e d can show that something already happened. It has different sounds in jumped, played, and wanted. The spelling stays e d.

lessons.name: Two words make one
lessons.intro: A compound word joins two words. Sun and set make sunset. Rain and coat make raincoat. Find the two words, then read the whole word. Tap a word to hear it. Read the whole word aloud.
lessons.rule: A compound word joins two words. Sun and set make sunset. Rain and coat make raincoat. Find the two words, then read the whole word.

lessons.name: Beginnings with meaning
lessons.intro: A prefix goes at the start of a word and changes its meaning. Un can mean not. Re can mean again. Listen to unfair and replay.
lessons.rule: A prefix goes at the start of a word and changes its meaning. Un can mean not. Re can mean again. Listen to unfair and replay.

items.prompt: What does unfair mean?
items.explanation: Un means not. Unfair means not fair.

items.prompt: What does replay mean?
items.explanation: Re means again. Replay means play again.

items.prompt: What does reread mean?
items.explanation: Reread means read again.

items.prompt: What does unsafe mean?
items.explanation: Unsafe means not safe.

items.prompt: What does refill mean?
items.explanation: Refill means fill again.

items.prompt: What does unkind mean?
items.explanation: Unkind means not kind.

lessons.name: Endings with meaning
lessons.intro: A suffix goes at the end of a word. Ful can mean full of or having. Less can mean without. Helpful means giving help. Fearless means without fear.
lessons.rule: A suffix goes at the end of a word. Ful can mean full of or having. Less can mean without. Helpful means giving help. Fearless means without fear.

items.prompt: What does helpful mean?
items.explanation: A helpful person gives help.

items.prompt: What does fearless mean?
items.explanation: Less means without. Fearless means without fear.

items.prompt: What does colourful mean?
items.explanation: Colourful means having lots of colour.

items.prompt: What does careless mean?
items.explanation: Careless means not taking care.

items.prompt: What does hopeful mean?
items.explanation: Hopeful means having hope.

items.prompt: What does powerless mean?
items.explanation: Powerless means without power.

lessons.name: Words in a sentence
lessons.intro: A sentence can help you work out a word. Listen for clues around a word you do not know. Try a meaning and check that the sentence still makes sense.
lessons.rule: A sentence can help you work out a word. Listen for clues around a word you do not know. Try a meaning and check that the sentence still makes sense.

items.prompt: The tiny kitten fit in one hand. What does tiny mean?
items.explanation: Fitting in one hand is a clue that tiny means very small.

items.prompt: The huge box would not fit through the door. What does huge mean?
items.explanation: Not fitting through the door is a clue that huge means very big.

items.prompt: We whispered in the quiet room. What does quiet mean?
items.explanation: Whispering is a clue. Quiet means not noisy.

items.prompt: The damp socks felt wet. What does damp mean?
items.explanation: Wet is a clue. Damp means slightly wet.

items.prompt: Mia was thrilled when her friend arrived. She smiled and jumped. What does thrilled mean?
items.explanation: Smiling and jumping are clues that thrilled means very excited.

items.prompt: The path was narrow. We had to walk in one line. What does narrow mean?
items.explanation: Walking in one line is a clue that narrow means not wide.

lessons.name: Little stories
lessons.intro: Read useful words with your grown-up first. Read each story twice, then answer the questions. You can hear a model reading if you need help. Tap a word to hear it. Read the whole word aloud.
lessons.rule: Read useful words with your grown-up first. Read each story twice, then answer the questions. You can hear a model reading if you need help.

stories.title: Sam and the cat
lines: Sam has a cat.
The cat is on a mat.
Sam can pat the cat.
The cat can nap.
stories.preview: Read together first: Sam, has, a, the, is, on.

stories.title: The red cup
lines: Ben has a red cup.
The cup is in a bag.
Ben can get the cup.
Ben can sip.
stories.preview: Read together first: Ben, has, a, the, is, in.

stories.title: At the shop
lines: Chad is at the shop.
The shop has a red sock.
Chad can get the sock.
The sock is in a bag.
stories.preview: Read together first: Chad, is, at, the, has, a, in.

questions.q: Where is the sock at the end?

stories.title: The duck
lines: A duck is in a pond.
The duck can dip.
A fish is in the pond.
The fish can dash.
stories.preview: Read together first: a, is, in, the, can. Pond has a blend at the end.

questions.q: What else is in the pond?

stories.title: The flag
lines: Glen has a flag.
The flag is in a tent.
Glen can grab the flag.
Glen can run with it.
stories.preview: Read together first: Glen, has, a, the, is, in, can, with, it.

questions.q: Where is the flag at first?
What can Glen do with the flag?

stories.title: The frog
lines: A frog is on a log.
The frog can jump.
The frog jumps in a pond.
Splash! The frog is wet.
stories.preview: Read together first: a, is, on, the, can. Preview jumps and splash together.

questions.q: Where is the frog at first?
How is the frog at the end?

stories.title: The raincoat
lines: Rain tapped on the window as Ava packed her bag.
She put a raincoat beside the door.
When she stepped outside, the raincoat kept her shirt dry.
She smiled and walked to school.
stories.preview: Preview together: Ava, window, beside, outside, walked, school. Focus: silent e, vowel teams, and compound words.

questions.q: What did Ava put beside the door?
questions.explanation: The second sentence says she put a raincoat beside the door.

questions.q: Why did Ava take the raincoat?
questions.explanation: It was raining, and the story says the raincoat kept her shirt dry.
The rain at the window is described before Ava goes outside.

stories.title: The lost lunchbox
lines: Noah looked in his bag for his lunchbox.
It was not there, so he checked beside his desk.
His friend pointed to a blue box on the shelf.
Noah found his lunchbox and thanked his friend.
stories.preview: Preview together: Noah, looked, checked, pointed, shelf, thanked. Focus: compounds, endings, and using clues.

questions.explanation: The first sentence says Noah looked for his lunchbox.
The friend pointed to a blue box on the shelf.

questions.q: Which word best describes the friend?
questions.explanation: The friend helped Noah find something he needed, so helpful fits.

stories.title: Seeds in a pot
lines: Lena filled a small pot with soil and planted seeds.
She put the pot near a window and gave it water.
For several days, the soil looked just the same.
Then a tiny green shoot pushed up through the soil.
stories.preview: Preview together: Lena, soil, planted, several, shoot, through. Informational topic: growing a plant.

questions.explanation: The first sentence says Lena planted seeds.

questions.q: What does tiny mean in this passage?
questions.explanation: Tiny describes the new shoot as very small.

questions.q: Which detail shows that the plant started to grow?
questions.explanation: The green shoot coming through the soil is evidence of new growth.

stories.title: A better bridge
lines: Eli made a bridge from blocks for his toy truck.
The first bridge fell when the truck rolled across it.
Eli added wide blocks under the middle of the bridge.
This time, the truck crossed and the bridge stayed up.
stories.preview: Preview together: Eli, bridge, blocks, truck, rolled, crossed. Focus: problem, solution, and evidence.

questions.q: What was the problem with the first bridge?
answers: It fell when the truck crossed.
questions.explanation: The second sentence says the first bridge fell.

answers: He added blocks under the middle.
questions.explanation: Eli added wide blocks under the middle of the bridge.

questions.q: How do we know the change helped?
questions.explanation: The bridge staying up when the truck crossed shows that the change helped.

prompts.listen: Listen to the word. Tap the word that matches.
prompts.build: Listen to the word. Use the letter tiles to build it. Then tap check.
prompts.read: Read the word aloud. Listen to the three choices. Pick the one that matches.
prompts.correct: Yes! You got it. Read the whole word aloud.
prompts.story-correct: Yes! The story tells you that.
prompts.retry: Not quite. Listen again. Take your time and try another answer.
prompts.story-retry: Read the story again. Find the part that answers the question.
prompts.hint: Listen again. Look at the letters from left to right. You can tap show the word if you need more help.
prompts.show: Here is the word. Read it aloud, then try again.
prompts.finish: Nice work! You finished this practice. You can try it again, or choose another lesson.
prompts.teach-demo: Let's try one together. Listen to the word. Tap the word that matches. You can use a hint.
prompts.story-directions: Read the story aloud. You can tap listen to hear it. Then answer the question. Tap the small play buttons if you want to hear the answers.
prompts.empty: Put the letters in the boxes first. Then tap check.
prompts.welcome: Welcome to Reading Room. Pick a lesson. Start with words you have learned with your grown-up.
prompts.rhyme: Listen to the question. Listen to each choice. Choose the word with the same ending sound.
prompts.quiz: Listen to the question. Choose the best answer. You can hear each answer before you choose.
prompts.quiz-correct: Yes. Listen to why that answer works.
prompts.quiz-retry: Not quite. Listen to the question and the choices again. Look for the clue.
prompts.reread: Read this passage aloud. Try it once, then read it again. Notice where each sentence ends. You can listen to a model if you need help.
prompts.review: These words needed another try. Let's practise them again in a new activity.
